published_source: Authors' Stata log logs/2_stata_regressions.smcl and esttab output tables/TABLE_04_pre_post_log_market_value_control_assets.tex in the package; no article text or PDF in the project, so the values are checked against the authors' code output only, not against the printed article.
notes: PROTOCOL 5c controls analysis. Table 4 (5) Year API < 2012: reghdfe ln_mkt_val ln_assets_total api_treat_post if is.na(api_treat_year) | api_treat_year < 2012, absorb(gvkey date) vce(cluster gvkey) (replication_package_MS-INS-22-01020/programs/2_stata_regressions.do line 946) on api_compustat_clean.dta, i.e. the Table 1 data after the same prep and the hacks merge (saved at line 308). Same sample definition as the matching Table 1 column; the only violation of the main rules is the time-varying control ln_assets_total = log(assets_total + 1) (line 127; missing for 266 of the authors' 133,303 rows), entered linearly as published. fixest on the authors' row-level sample reproduces b = 0.3053508, SE = 0.0912333, N = 129402 (exact; assets coefficient 0.738 in column 1). Total assets is a plausible mediator of API-driven growth (adding it cuts the Table 1 coefficient by about two thirds), so the spec is flagged mediator_controls as in the batch-G 5c ruling. Outcome SD in the controls regression sample = 2.45547. Data: shipped analysis_dataset/api_compustat_gvkey_quarterly_sictreated.dta (Compustat x ProgrammableWeb firm-quarters, original data), rebuilt in R following 2_stata_regressions.do lines 121-262: drop if ln_mkt_val missing or sic_code empty (133,292 firm-quarters, 4,748 firms, 2007Q1-2020Q3 = Stata %tq 188-242, 55 quarters); date = quarterly(year, quarter); api_treat_date_q = qofd(api_treat_date); sinceAPIq = date - api_treat_date_q; dmerge gvkey dateq using hacks.dta (1:m, _merge == 2 dropped) adds 11 duplicate firm-quarters (11 firm-quarters each matched to two PRC breach events; 133,303 rows). Prepared file ~/did_packages/_work/mnsc.2023.4968/api_panel_collapsed.rds collapses the 11 merge duplicates to one row per firm-quarter (outcome = mean of the duplicated rows; all other columns identical within the duplicates) with frequency weight w_mergedup = number of authors' rows (2 for 11 firm-quarters, 1 otherwise). This reproduces the authors' row-level OLS exactly (identical normal equations and cluster scores) while giving the runner a proper firm-quarter panel: with the duplicates kept, estimators.R's anyDuplicated(id, t) > 0 test would switch CSA to the repeated-cross-section att_gt(panel = FALSE) path for a firm panel. The authors' row-level sample is kept in api_panel_authors_sample.rds. Treatment: gvar = api_treat_date_q (quarter of first public API); api_treat_post equals 1[date >= api_treat_date_q] in every row (verified), 0 for the 4,569 never-adopters, absorbing (no switch-offs). Full sample: 179 adopters with 50 distinct adoption quarters (2005-2019); 100 switchers in 41 cohorts observed before and after adoption; 74 adopters treated at their first observed quarter (always-treated; 16 adopted before 2007Q1 and are dated at 2007Q1 by run_spec's gvar mapping); 5 adopt after their last observation. Never-treated firms: 96.2% of firms, 95.0% of rows. Unbalanced panel (entry/exit), so run_spec uses the composition-fixed CSA cells. Cluster gvkey as published. reghdfe drops 101 singletons (published N); run_spec keeps them (same point estimate).
